q: Montréal is built on what kind of land?
funFact: The whole city sits on an island in the St. Lawrence River.

q: The city of Montréal is named after which hill?
funFact: Mont Royal means "royal mountain" in French.

q: Which language do most people speak in Montréal?
funFact: Most people in Montréal speak English too, so say bonjour first.

q: What is Montréal's underground train system called?
funFact: The Montréal Metro opened in 1966 and has four coloured lines.

q: How many white flowers are on the Québec flag?
funFact: Those flowers are called fleurs-de-lis, and they sit on blue.

q: What is the little lake on top of Mount Royal called?
funFact: In French it is Lac aux Castors — the same thing.

q: Montréal is the biggest city in which province?
funFact: Québec City is the capital, but Montréal has more people.

q: Québec stop signs say ARRÊT. What does that mean?
funFact: Watch for it — you will see arrêt signs all week.

q: Mount Royal Park was designed by the same person as New York's Central Park. Who?
funFact: He liked winding paths so the walk feels gentle uphill.

q: How do you say "thank you" in French?
funFact: Say merci beaucoup when you mean thank you very much.
